Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 26-year-old with 3 days of worsening headache, diffuse but maximal right periorbital; photophobia; transient visual phenomena at onset; nausea without vomiting; no focal neurologic deficits; no fever; no head trauma. Family history positive for migraines. Features are most consistent with migraine with aura per DDx and transcript.
- Red flags screened: no focal neurologic deficits, no fever, no rash, no trauma. Neck pain/stiffness response was inconsistent (patient initially said “yeah,” then “no”)—conflict noted.
- Alternative considerations per DDx: tension-type headache (some features overlap but photophobia/aura less typical); cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (low likelihood given clinical picture; social smoking noted; oral contraceptive status unknown).
- Plan discussed: optimize analgesia; consider stronger anti-inflammatory and adjunct analgesics; maintain headache diary; follow-up in 1–2 weeks; earlier review if worsening or neurologic/visual symptoms.

Management Plan
- Optimize NSAID regimen: advise correct ibuprofen dosing (up to two tablets, three times daily; specific tablet strength not documented).
- Prescribe Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Adjunct analgesia: Paracetamol and/or Codeine discussed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Headache diary to track frequency, severity, potential triggers (e.g., light, screen use, stress).
- Workplace/behavioral: continue reduced screen brightness; consider breaks from screens as needed.
- Follow-up: return in 1–2 weeks; consider preventive therapy if headaches become frequent.
- Safety net: seek urgent care if worsening headache, new visual changes or loss, weakness, speech difficulty, fever, or if generally unwell.
- Vision: consider repeat eye test if eye strain persists (wears glasses; no recent exam).
- Clarify at follow-up: oral contraceptive use (asked but not documented).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Migraine with aura – High likelihood: unilateral periorbital predominance, photophobia, initial visual phenomena (“shooting lights”), nausea, family history, poor response to simple NSAID at suboptimal dosing.
- Tension-type headache – Moderate likelihood: dull, continuous ache and recent stress support; however, photophobia and visual aura are atypical.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis – Low likelihood: progressive headache in young woman; social smoking and unknown OCP status are potential risks, but absence of focal deficits and strong migraine features lower suspicion.
